sources.searcher_note: Bot-blocked (HTTP 403 to WebFetch and curl), not a true paywall; headline used as quote. Search snippet said DHS ran the most expensive political ad campaign of 2025, at least $51M per AdImpact, and that DHS disputes its ads are political. Snippet text not verified on page.

notes: Lead is pre_known (lead_cites_press). Plenty of coverage names DHS's 2025-26 ad campaign ($200M-$240M contracts, Noem, Strategy Group, Safe America Media: ProPublica, Bloomberg, The Hill, NewsNation, Senate Welch letters) but those are TV/contract stories, not Google. The only Google-specific coverage found: NOTUS citing Google's ad transparency center ($297,100 YouTube in Oct 2025) and Jayapal/Balint letter ($3M Google/YouTube). No source found stating that Google filed DHS as a political/election advertiser, that DHS is the only federal agency in Google's political ad data, the $5.29M total, or the #3-of-2025 rank. Axios (AdImpact, all platforms) calls it the year's most expensive political ad campaign and says DHS disputes the ads are political: that is the closest disagreement found. Daily Beast 2019 story on Facebook/Instagram labeling DHS recruitment ads political exists but is Meta, not Google, so not recorded. No coverage dated after 2026-06-30 found. Axios fetch via web.archive.org and curl both failed from here.
